claim: A hint that contradicts the solver's false view roughly doubles the solve rate against a hint that agrees with it (59% vs 26%, d=0.64, N=30, 572 valid trials, magic tricks). Agreeing hints add nothing.
agent_test: On stuck tasks, give a retry either an error message naming the clashing assumption or a generic 'try again' / an agreeing restatement, same token budget; compare solve rate.

claim: Insight difficulty has two separable sources: how wide the constraint to relax is, and how tight the chunk to break is. Matchstick medians were A 40 s, B 155 s, C 300 s (cap), D 140 s, and solve rates A 23/24, C 18/24, B 9/24 in a second study with eye tracking.
agent_test: Write O6 as two moves (relax a stated rule; split a unit / re-tokenise). Ablate each on tasks built to need one or the other, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Telling solvers that a normally forbidden form is allowed makes the hard items easy (tautology-first group solved all tautological Type C in Block 1; later regular Type C 92% vs 94%). Relaxation can be supplied from outside.
agent_test: Give the model an explicit list of constraints that may be dropped on a puzzle where one hidden constraint blocks the answer; compare with no list.

claim: After one solved hard item, the same type becomes as easy as the easiest type within the session (transfer B p<.05, C p<.001, none for A). What transfers is the relaxed constraint, not surface similarity.
agent_test: Store 'assumption X was wrong' after a solved impasse and offer it first on a later same-type task; compare with no stored lesson. Check for harm on different-type tasks.

claim: Impasse is not a single event. Only 49% of solvers (19/39) and 13% of non-solvers (8/62) followed the classic search-impasse-insight-search order; search and impasse recurred in half of solvers.
agent_test: Allow the stuck detector to fire more than once per task and cap total reframes; compare with a one-shot reframe at equal tokens.

claim: People cannot report their own impasse or progress reliably. Reports of impasse did not rise during behaviourally defined impasse; warmth ratings did not separate insight from non-insight solutions; confident insight solutions can be wrong and stick.
agent_test: Compare a stuck detector driven by code (repeat count, stalled test output) with one driven by asking the model 'are you stuck?'; report precision and recall against human-marked stalls.

claim: Relaxing the wrong constraint is not enough. In the ten-penny problem, line/intersection hints worked only with a search criterion (maximise intersections); maximization raised success (OR 2.18) but 28% still failed.
agent_test: After a reframe, add a score to search against and a rule that attempts must differ; compare with reframe alone.

claim: Incubation or sleep does not raise restructuring: no effect in magic tricks and classic insight problems (N=77, incubation p=.93, sleep p=.83). The positive REM result on the RAT (Cai 2009) was not tested here.
agent_test: Compare a blind restart (fresh context, same prompt) with a restart that carries a changed frame, at equal tokens.

claim: The brain map for insight and conflict is not settled. Danek found conflict in posterior visual areas, thalamus and hippocampus, not mainly in ACC. Earlier work (Luo 2004, Dietrich and Kanso) favours ACC, and Qin 2009 argues ACC marks subgoal handling after a candidate appears.
agent_test: None. Do not build design on region claims; use behavioural triggers.

claim: A fast mismatch signal exists when a solution breaks the first reading: N380 at Cz with ACC dipole, 14 subjects, 120 riddles. Small N, confounded with difficulty and surprise.
agent_test: None directly. It motivates a cheap check run right after the output appears, not after a long rumination.

claim: Models that review their own answer without an external signal do not improve and often get worse (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over two rounds; Gemini 1.5 Flash MATH500 52.6 to 41.4). Past gains used oracle labels.
agent_test: Run S6 with (a) a code-found failure, (b) a self-judged 'maybe wrong' trigger, (c) no revision; report all three with no oracle in the stop rule, at equal tokens.

claim: The bottleneck is locating the conflict, not fixing it. With the true mistake location, backtracking added +18.04 to +43.92 points on wrong traces; GPT-4 found the mistake in only 52.87% overall. Oracle labels lifted GPT-4 HotpotQA 49 to 59.
agent_test: Compare repair prompts that name the failing step (from a test or diff) with repair prompts that say only 'something is wrong'.

claim: Models correct an injected error when it is attributed to the user but miss the identical error attributed to themselves (64.5% blind spot across 14 non-reasoning models). Appending 'Wait' cut it by 89.3%. Gap search: in Tsui v3, reasoning-mode models show a small or negative blind spot, and 'Wait' on non-thinking Qwen3-14B lifts 0.117 to 0.868 (thinking mode 0.843); the effect belongs to non-reasoning mode.
agent_test: At check time, present the draft as another author's work versus as the model's own; compare error catch rate.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace 'Aha' shifts in small RL-trained models are rare (6.31% of traces) and linked to lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44% for Qwen2.5-1.5B). They do not become useful with more training.
agent_test: Count self-initiated 'wait, reconsider' events in our agent traces and compare accuracy with and without them.

claim: A cue added by code helps where model-initiated doubt does not: a reconsideration cue under high entropy gave +8.41 pp on MATH-500 (0.3221 to 0.4062), only +0.45 pp on crosswords and +0.01 pp on Rush Hour; 'Wait' appended cut the blind spot 89.3%. Part of the gain may be extra compute. Gap search: Ghosal 2025 finds a blind 'Wait' extension loses to parallel samples at equal tokens (GSM8K 1.5B model: -11.8% vs +10.1%), while s1 shows small Wait gains (AIME24 50.0 to 56.7 at 4x). No compute-matched test of a gated cue on frontier models exists.
agent_test: Gate a code-inserted reconsideration cue on sample disagreement or failing check; compare with a second plain sample at equal tokens.

claim: Models often produce the right answer in their thought log and then do not endorse it: verification failures were 5.23% to 39.34% of wrong answers across models with usable logs (Claude Opus 4 25.00%). On NazoNazo riddles non-reasoning models scored 7.6% and reasoning models 17.6% against a human 52.9%.
agent_test: Have code collect every candidate answer from the trace and run a held-out check on each; compare with the model's own final pick.

claim: Familiar-but-wrong cues fixate non-reasoning LLMs. Only Connect walls: GPT-4 solved 6 walls with red herrings, 68 with fewer, 471 with none. M-ARC: best models about 50% vs physicians 66%. MedEinst: trap rate 43-61%. More in-context examples did not help.
agent_test: Re-run a failed task after removing the first failed grouping or showing no prior failed frame; compare with showing it.

claim: Newer reasoning models close much of the fixation gap: on M-ARC the best reasoning model reached 0.751 (physicians 0.66; earlier best 50%). NazoNazo still shows a large gap for most reasoning models (17.6%), with GPT-5 the exception.
agent_test: Test the scaffold on a reasoning-model baseline, not only a non-reasoning one; headroom may be smaller than older numbers suggest.

claim: Models favour evidence that matches their memory and are sensitive to evidence order (over 5% answer change in most models, over 30% for PaLM2 and Llama2-7B). They accept a counter-answer when it is coherent and the only evidence.
agent_test: Show a failing result as one coherent contradiction in fixed order; test both orders and compare.

claim: Debate among same-model agents does not fix a dominant wrong prior: on MedEinst, MDAgent and DyLAN reached about 8-10% robust accuracy, while the authors' evidence-audit scaffold reached 24.21% (base 11.86%). Agreeing samples are not a conflict signal.
agent_test: Compare majority vote of same-model samples with a code-run counterfactual pair test (change the one deciding fact) at equal tokens.

claim: A coded failure trigger plus stored reflection improves agent loops (Reflexion: 130/134 ALFWorld, HumanEval 91%) when the failure signal is reliable; external feedback is what makes self-correction work in the surveys.
agent_test: Compare reflect-on-code-failure with reflect-every-turn at equal tokens on tasks that have a runnable check.

claim: A review prompt itself pushes models toward changing the answer (CommonSenseQA drop; Gemini Flash right-to-wrong 15.8% before SCoRe training vs 1.4% after). Needless flips of right answers are a main cost. Gap search: Huang's default prompt was already neutral ('could be either correct or incorrect') and still lost accuracy; three wordings all failed to beat the first answer.
agent_test: Make code adopt a revision only if the check improves; count flips of right answers with and without that rule.

claim: Handling the problem physically does not automatically aid restructuring. A Bayesian conceptual replication on matchstick algebra found no rise in movements or success when a condition was made interactive; movement hurt high-level constraint relaxation.
agent_test: None. Match the aid to the source of difficulty rather than adding generic interaction.

claim: Irrelevant or clashing context drops math accuracy; no more than 18% of baseline-solved problems stayed solved across all distractor types; self-consistency recovered recall to 99.7% and an 'ignore irrelevant information' line helped partly.
agent_test: Sample several answers then select with a code check; compare with a single answer plus an ignore-distractors line.

claim: Stuck-loop detection in code is cheap and measured in one study: a 3-gram repeat detector flagged 100% of one model's no-submit tasks with no false positives on two other models, but it only sees stalls, not confident wrong fixes. The production harness (window 20, pause at 3 repeats) reports no gain of its own.
agent_test: Measure precision and recall of the repeat-count trigger against human-marked stalls, and the added value of a mismatch trigger.

claim: Extending one trace with a blind 'Wait' loses to independent samples at equal tokens in small distilled reasoning models (accuracy 87.3% at 1100 tokens falling to 70.3% at 15980; at a 16K budget parallel is about 22% above Wait-and-Think-More). The pro-Wait evidence (s1) compares different models, so it is not an equal-token test.
agent_test: Run cue vs no cue vs second plain sample at the same total tokens on a frontier reasoning model; gate the cue on a failing check.

claim: A model-internal confidence signal can pick out bad traces and save tokens: DeepConf cut generated tokens by up to 84.7% at equal or better accuracy; GPT-OSS-120B AIME25 99.9 vs 97.0 majority. Aggressive filtering can hurt where the model is confidently wrong (HMMT25 92.9 to 88.9).
agent_test: Compare token entropy or low-confidence windows with a failing test as the S6 trigger, at equal tokens.

claim: A wrong frame is often repeated, so sample agreement cannot flag it: in coding agents, 68% to 80% of failing runs for two models were 5/5 submitted and 0/5 resolved, with near-identical patches (embedding cosine 0.80 to 0.91 vs 0.48 to 0.57). Two pre-edit 'check your reading' prompts did not move resolve rate (Claude 65.2 to 64.8; GPT-5 44.4 to 46.0 and 44.0).
agent_test: Use an external test or a frame-level contrast as the trigger, not agreement between samples; measure it on tasks with known wrong frames.

claim: The self-correction blind spot is mainly a non-reasoning-mode effect in open models: reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot (Tsui v3), and 'Wait' on a non-thinking base nearly matches its reasoning sibling (DeepSeek-V3 0.567 to 0.902 vs R1 0.908). Red-herring fixation on riddles still remains (K18).
agent_test: Retest the blind spot, red-herring fixation and verification failure on the frontier model the agent will use, not on the 2023 baselines.

claim: A neutral review wording does not remove the loss from intrinsic self-review in weaker models. GPT-4-Turbo GSM8K 91.5 to 88.0/90.0 (neutral), 90.0/90.0, 91.0/91.0; Llama-2 CSQA 64.0 to 37.5/36.5 (neutral), 26.0/37.0, 24.0/43.0. Wording shifts results by several points (GPT-4-Turbo CSQA round 1: 81.5, 74.5, 81.5). The 'false options look relevant' explanation remains untested.
agent_test: Keep a code-side rule: adopt a revision only when a check improves; test two review wordings for flip rate on right answers.

claim: Stored lessons from failures transfer modestly and can harm. ReasoningBank: SWE-Bench-Verified 34.2 to 38.8 (flash); WebArena Multi +4.6 over the best baseline where AWM fell below no-memory; AWM 44.4 to 42.2 when failures were added. Trace2Skill: +57.65 pp best cell, but negative cells, and an official skill hurt a smaller agent. EDV: held-out tau2 Pass@1 85.1 vs 76.4 without memory. None tests a single 'assumption X was wrong' lesson on a different task type.
agent_test: Store each lesson with an applicability condition; A/B same-type vs different-type later tasks and count harm.

claim: Agent self-written lessons can store the agent's own mistake as guidance (Self-Confirmation Trap Rate 11.0% under reflection memory, 5.0% with third-party distillation and unanimous review). A confident new frame can therefore be stored as truth.
agent_test: Admit a lesson to memory only after a code check or a different model confirms it.

claim: Incomplete input is a real, separate LLM failure from a wrong frame. Giving matchstick equations as text instead of images raised o3 from 38.50 to 60.00 (all levels up; Gemini-2.5-Pro 22.50 to 45.25). Wrong-frame failures are a different pattern (K28), and only one of them was fixed by adding information. Whether these map to Kaplan-Simon vs Ohlsson accounts is a hypothesis.
agent_test: Tag each stall as missing information or wrong frame; try add-information first, change-frame second, and compare repair rates.

claim: Models act on hints placed in the prompt but rarely say so: chain of thought verbalised the hint in 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (R1) of cases where the hint was used. An injected relaxation hint can change behaviour without showing in the model's own account. No LLM test of the Knoblich Exp 3 analogue (which constraint may be relaxed) was found.
agent_test: Test a relaxation hint on lateral or matchstick items with a no-hint control; log hint injection in code.
